sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Hello-Agents is a free, open course from the Datawhale community on building AI agents from scratch. Its 16 chapters go from what an agent is, through classic patterns like ReAct, to memory, protocols, training and full projects.
sixtySeconds.problem: Agent tutorials are scattered and often stop at using a low-code tool. Hello-Agents teaches the ideas underneath, has you build your own agent framework on the OpenAI API, and finishes with real case studies.
whoFor: Developers and students with some programming experience
Engineers moving from low-code agent tools to code
Learners preparing for agent-related job interviews
Readers of Chinese or English (both editions exist)
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a structured, theory-plus-practice path through agents with runnable code for every chapter. It is a course, not a library you install in production.
requirements: A web browser to read online
Git and Python to run the chapter code
An LLM API key for the hands-on chapters

overview: The course has five parts. Part 1 covers agent basics, history and language model fundamentals. Part 2 is hands-on: implementing ReAct, Plan-and-Solve and Reflection, trying low-code platforms like Coze, Dify and n8n, using frameworks such as AutoGen, AgentScope and LangGraph, and building your own framework.

Part 3 extends that framework with memory and retrieval, context engineering, communication protocols (MCP, A2A, ANP), agentic reinforcement learning from SFT to GRPO, and evaluation. Part 4 builds a travel assistant, a deep research agent and a simulated cyber town, and Part 5 is a capstone project.

You can read it online, download a free PDF from the releases page, or clone the repository. All supporting code is in the code folder, and the authors strongly recommend running and debugging it yourself. Community extra chapters cover interview questions, Agent Skills, GUI and web agents.
